Title: Queen visits man who lost wife, two sons in Kluang house fire
Article:
KLUANG: Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, today visited a man who lost his wife and two sons in a devastating house fire in Taman Titiwangsa here.
Her Majesty, accompanied by Her Highness Tunku Mahkota Johor Che' Puan Mahkota Khaleeda Bustamam, visited Khairul Nizam Wahid, 50, and offered support and aid to the grieving family.
The royal visit came after the fire claimed the lives of
Khairul Nizam's wife and their two children
on Sept 9.
Raja Zarith Sofiah and Che' Puan Khaleeda also visited three other recipients and presented them with aid during their visit to the district.
The assistance was part of aid provided by the Queen to asnaf recipients in Kluang.
The recipients included Saimah Samijan, Rajaswary Sakarai and Loh Yee Teng, according to a post on the Royal Johor Facebook page.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: After toddler attack, Batu Pahat steps up stray dog crackdown
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A child's recent encounter with stray dogs in Peserai has triggered a wider crackdown, with the local council stepping up operations in villages and known hotspots across the district.
The Batu Pahat Municipal Council (MPBP) has captured 736 stray dogs in 205 operations this year, following 1,557 captures in 263 operations last year.
MPBP has also intensified efforts to remove roaming dogs from high-risk areas.
On Sept 5, two-year-old
Nur Haira Watikah Mohammad Hamizi was attacked
by five stray dogs at about 7am outside her grandmother's house in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, here.
She suffered severe injuries to almost her entire body, was placed in an induced coma and underwent surgery.
The council has stepped up operations at the site of the attack while widening patrols and dog-catching efforts to nearby villages and other identified hotspots.
MPBP president Mohd Nazid Jasiman said
736 stray dogs had been captured
in 205 operations across the district as of Aug 31 this year.
This followed 1,557 dogs captured in 263 operations throughout last year.
He said regular patrols would continue at locations identified as having stray dog problems, with enforcement action also taken following complaints from the public.
Among the hotspots identified last year were Taman Putera Indah, Batu Pahat town centre, Taman Sri Gading, Taman Universiti and Taman Bukit Perdana.
This year, Parit Raja, Taman Putera Indah and Taman Evergreen Heights have emerged as hotspots.
The intensified action comes amid growing concern over public safety, as roaming dogs can pose a risk to pedestrians, particularly children, while packs may also become aggressive when defending territory or food.
Nazid said the captured dogs would be managed according to the Housing and Local Government Ministry's standard operating procedures under the Trap-Reclaim-Rehome-Dispose approach (TRRD).
The TRRD approach involves capturing stray dogs, allowing owners to reclaim them, rehoming suitable animals and, as a last resort, humane disposal of those that cannot be rehomed.
The council would also strengthen public awareness campaigns, dog licensing and responsible pet ownership initiatives.
For a longer-term solution, MPBP is developing its Stray Animal Control Action Plan 2027-2031, covering population control, licensing, enforcement, public education, adoption and neutering.
The plan will also involve cooperation with the Veterinary Services Department, local communities and animal welfare organisations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 30 inmates find purpose through Quran memorisation programme in Machang
Article:
MACHANG: Thirty inmates at Machang Rehabilitation Centre are taking part in a structured tahfiz programme, with two having completed memorising all 30 juzuk of the Quran and another two expected to do so by year-end.
Its director Ahmad Zulkarnain Abdul Khalid said Sekolah Tahfiz Al-Quran Al-Furqan, established in 2023 in collaboration with the Kelantan Islamic Religious and Malay Customs Council (MAIK), was the first organised tahfiz school provided within a prison facility in the country.
He said the programme had received strong support from MAIK and was formally registered, giving inmates the opportunity to pursue Quranic memorisation in a structured learning environment.
"Currently, 30 inmates are taking part in the programme. Two of them have already completed the memorisation of all 30 juzuk of the Quran.
"By the end of this year, we expect another two inmates to complete all 30 juzuk," he said.
Zulkarnain said the programme was part of efforts to provide inmates with a meaningful rehabilitation process by combining correctional programmes with religious education.
He said while similar tahfiz initiatives existed in other prisons, some were still in the process of strengthening their operations and programmes.
Machang Rehabilitation Centre is a correctional facility run by the Prisons Department in Kelantan, focusing on inmate rehabilitation, skills training and employment
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iraq to reopen Iran crossings after drone attack
Article:
BAGHDAD: Iraqi authorities announced on Sunday a timeline to reopen three crossings with Iran, a day after closing them following a drone attack originating from their shared border on a Saudi pipeline.
After the Friday night attack on the East-West pipeline, Baghdad sacked the military commander in Missan province near the Iran border, after authorities determined the drones were launched from there.
The government then closed three crossings, citing the need to reorganise operations and boost intelligence efforts to stop violations.
Two Iraqi security sources told AFP on Saturday that drone launchers were found near the al-Shib border crossing in Missan.
The government's security media cell said Sunday that "after reviewing operations at the border crossings," they would gradually reopen for passengers and trade on a timeline from Sunday until Thursday.
The crossings are Shalamsheh in Basra, al-Shib in Missan, and al-Mandali in Diyala.
Shalamsheh and al-Shib reopened to passengers on Sunday but not to trade, the government media cell said.
No group has claimed responsibility for the attack, and an alliance of Iran-backed Iraqi armed factions said they hadn't struck the pipeline, though Riyadh had previously accused Iraqi groups of targeting its oil infrastructure.
In July, the United States and Saudi Arabia said they had struck Iran-backed fighters in Iraq in response to attacks on US forces and Saudi oil facilities.
Pro-Iran armed groups have supported Teheran during the Middle East war, claiming hundreds of attacks on US bases in Iraq and across the region.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran authorities say one dead after ship struck in Hormuz
Article:
TEHERAN: A ship was struck in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, killing one person and injuring three, local Iranian authorities said, as Teheran and Washington clash over the strategic waterway.
"A merchant vessel was struck around 5am (0130 GMT) this morning off the coasts of Hengam and Qeshm islands. One person was killed and three others were injured," Qeshm city governor Amir Teymouri said, according to state TV, without specifying the origin of the strike.
Several explosions were reported overnight around Qeshm, the largest island in the Hormuz strait.
The UK Maritime Trade Operations monitor said later it had received reports of a vessel being struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.
"A fire has broken out onboard the vessel following the reported attack. Local authorities are on the scene and assisting in evacuating crew members," it added without elaborating further on the attack.
The incident comes a day before a meeting between Iran and Gulf states in Oman, which also borders the strait, over the blockaded route crucial for global oil and gas trade.
Control over the strait has become a major flashpoint in the conflict between Iran and the United States in their six-month war.
In retaliation for attacks by the United States and Israel that started the war on February 28, Iran has blocked the waterway, a passage that was previously free and unobstructed before the conflict began.
Iran now requires vessels to obtain authorisation to pass through the strait, citing security and sovereignty concerns, and is considering a mechanism to impose service fees.
Vessels that fail to comply are frequently targeted by Iranian strikes, while the United States sporadically bombs the Iranian coast in a bid to challenge Teheran's control of the strait.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Remains of Captain Zainol Afiq arrive at Bandar Baru Senawang mosque
Article:
SEREMBAN: The remains of helicopter crash victim Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham arrived at Bandar Baru Senawang Mosque here about 4.20pm today.
Family members, friends and members of the public had gathered at the mosque from about 4pm to await the arrival of the pilot's remains.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan was also at the mosque, arriving at about 4.15pm.
The mosque compound and surrounding areas were packed with vehicles, resembling the scene during Friday prayers.
Traffic police were deployed to manage traffic, while Seremban district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Yatim Osman and his personnel monitored the situation.
Zainol Afiq is expected to be buried at the Forest Heights Muslim Cemetery here after the funeral prayers.
On Tuesday, a helicopter crashed near
Long Lellang in Sarawak
while carrying out a healthcare mission to remote parts of the state, killing all five people on board, including four medical personnel.
The other victims were Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, and nurses Jessie Paya Jok and Debra Moset.

Title: Helicopter crash: Remains of Dr Ainul Baraah laid to rest in Pengkalan Chepa
Article:
KOTA BARU: A sombre atmosphere enveloped the burial of medical officer the late Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 33, at Sri Kedeper Islamic Cemetery in Pengkalan Chepa here today.
The burial ceremony concluded at 2.20pm following the funeral prayer at Al Karomah Mosque in Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa, which was
led by Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad
immediately after the Zohor prayers.
Also present were Health Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad, Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud, Kelantan Health director Dr Kasuadi Hussin, as well as the deceased's family members and friends.
Earlier, a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) special aircraft carrying Dr Ainul Baraah's remains from Miri, Sarawak, arrived at the Sultan Ismail Petra Airport in Pengkalan Chepa, Kota Bharu, at 11.21am.
Dr Ainul Baraah, 33, was one of five victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Baram, Sarawak; the aircraft crashed and caught fire near the end of the Long Lellang STOLport runway at approximately 3.40 pm last Tuesday.
The crash also claimed the lives of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30, medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31, and two nurses, Jessie Paya Jok, 44, and Debra Moset, 40.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saifuddin welcomes Umno commitment to stay in unity government
Article:
KULIM: Umno's commitment to remain in the unity government until the end of its term is a positive development to ensure political stability, economic growth and efforts to address the people's problems remain priorities, a Pakatan Harapan leader said.
PH secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's stance was in line with the memorandum of understanding signed between the parties in 2022 to form the unity government.
He also said political attacks between leaders of both parties were normal and could be resolved ahead of the election.
"I was involved in the formation of the unity government as early as November 2022, and I know that, in terms of documentation, we signed an understanding, a written agreement, to work together until the end of the term.
"So when the Umno president said at his press conference yesterday that he would uphold that commitment, it is because, rationally, this government needs to be defended in the interest of political stability so that we can focus on managing the economy and ensuring the people benefit.
"I think that is a good decision and we welcome it," he said.
Saifuddin, who is also home minister, said this when met after attending a visit to the Kampung Badlishah-Ayer Putih, Junjong road construction and completion project here today.
On the criticism frequently directed by Umno leaders at PH, and vice versa, Saifuddin said such remarks could be based on issues that each party's leadership considered important.
He said the criticism had so far not affected the stability of the unity government, with cooperation between the parties remaining intact.
"Exchanging attacks is normal in politics. I agree, I say so. He does not agree, he says so. That is politics.
"What is most important is that its (Umno's) president has clearly said it will remain (in the unity government). We hold on to that first. As for the usual attacks, I do not consider them to be affecting stability," he said.
Yesterday, Zahid, at a press conference after the Umno General Assembly, reiterated the
party's commitment to continue supporting the existing leadership in the administration of the country.
He said Umno also did not oppose any party, particularly the Prime Minister, as the assembly's resolution to remain in the unity government until the end of the term must be respected.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dzulkefly leads 1,000 congregants in funeral prayers for Dr Ainul Baraah
Article:
KOTA BARU: Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad led the funeral prayers for medical officer, the late Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 33, at Al Karomah Mosque in Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa, here at 1.37 pm today.
The prayers were attended by over 1,000 congregants, including Ministry of Health (MOH) secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad, Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud, Kelantan State Health director Dr Kasuadi Hussin, as well as the deceased's family members and friends.
The deceased's father, Kamarudin Salleh, 69, said he and his family had granted permission for Dzulkefly to lead the funeral prayers as a mark of respect.
"I wish to express my gratitude to the Health Minister and the public—including relatives and friends—for their constant prayers and for keeping my late daughter in their thoughts," he said.
Earlier, a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) special aircraft carrying Dr Ainul Baraah's remains from Miri, Sarawak, arrived at Sultan Ismail Petra Airport, Pengkalan Chepa, at 11.21 am.
The crash on Tuesday claimed the lives of all five individuals on board the Bo-105 helicopter operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace after it crashed near the end of the Long Lellang STOLport runway at approximately 3.40 pm.
In addition to Dr Ainul Baraah, the other victims were Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and two nurses, Jessie Paya Jok, 44, and Debra Moset, 40.
– BERNAMA

Title: APEC ministers push for greater energy security in Asia Pacific
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) energy ministers are pushing to strengthen energy security across Asia Pacific as rising electricity demand puts greater pressure on power systems, costs and supply chains.
Electricity consumption across APEC could nearly double by 2060, driven by growing electrification, data centres and changing transport needs,
Meeting in Beijing for the 16th APEC Energy Ministerial Meeting, ministers focused on how the region can meet that demand while strengthening energy systems, widening access and limiting cost pressures on households and businesses.
"The Asia Pacific accounts for roughly 60 per cent of global energy production and consumption.
"Strengthening energy cooperation is directly relevant not only to each economy's own development but also carries significant weight for the global energy landscape." said Ding Xuexiang, China's vice premier, in his opening remarks.
Artificial intelligence (AI) is adding another dimension to the challenge.
In 2025, electricity demand for AI training data centers grew 17 per cent, outpacing the three percent growth in global electricity demand.
At the same time, AI can help energy systems forecast demand, manage grids and distribute power more efficiently.
Ministers highlighted the need for more energy-efficient technologies and talent capable of working across the energy and digital sectors, backed by strong cybersecurity and data protection.
But meeting new demand is only part of the challenge.
Ministers also focused on extending reliable electricity to underserved communities, including through off-grid and mini-grid systems that can bring power to remote areas without relying on extensions of the main grid.
"Energy is a critical foundation for economic and social development. We must jointly improve energy accessibility, delivering high-quality energy services and practical measures to help remote areas and vulnerable groups improve their energy situation," Ding urged.
Affordability was another focus, with ministers calling for easier access to financing that can help households cover the upfront cost of energy-efficient appliances and systems.
Economies also discussed how to meet technology-driven energy demand without increasing costs for local communities, emphasising consumer protection and more transparent rules for electricity pricing and trading.
Supply chain disruptions are also compounding affordability pressures, driving up prices and straining energy systems region-wide.
Ministers deliberated ways to diversify energy sources and trade routes, strengthen critical energy infrastructures such as submarine and power cables and enhance emergency reserve management across the region.
As the region's energy landscape shifts, resilience, access and affordability are converging into a single priority.
The meeting's discussions build on progress towards APEC's goal of doubling the region's share of renewable energy by 2030 and cutting energy intensity 45 per cent by 2035.
The meeting returned to Beijing 12 years after APEC energy ministers met in the city in 2014, when they set the region's 2030 renewable energy goal.
"Twelve years later, the global energy landscape is undergoing complex and profound transformations," said Wang Hongzhi, chair of the ministerial meeting and administrator of China's National Energy Administration.
"Patterns of energy production and consumption are being reshaped at an accelerated pace, presenting a new set of opportunities and challenges for energy development in the Asia-Pacific," Hongzhi added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Skeleton found inside water drum at Durian Tunggal Dam
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Skeletal remains believed to be human were found inside a water drum at the Durian Tunggal Dam catchment pond here at noon.
The discovery was made after a member of the public found the blue water drum and alerted authorities.
Alor Gajah District Police Chief Superintendent Ahmad Abu Bakar said the identity of the skeleton has yet to be established.
He said police are investigating to determine the cause of death and how the remains ended up inside the drum.
"The identity of the skeleton has yet to be established and investigations are ongoing to determine the cause of death and how it ended up inside the drum," he told reporters at the scene.
Further developments on the case are expected to be announced by police once initial investigations are complete.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lebuh Pudu raid uncovers suspected clinics serving foreigners
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: At least four premises suspected of illegally selling and storing medicines, including two operating like makeshift clinics for foreigners, were uncovered during a massive Immigration Department-led operation in Lebuh Pudu today.
The suspected clinics, concealed behind businesses selling textiles and offering travel services, were equipped with devices used to conduct blood pressure, blood sugar and blood tests.
Authorities believe the premises catered primarily to foreigners and were possibly operated by foreign doctors, although no one was found inside when enforcement officers raided them.
The discovery was made during Op Bersepadu Mega, a multi-agency operation led by the Immigration Department which saw 472 foreigners suspected of immigration offences detained following raids beginning at 11am.
Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya Health Department Pharmacy Enforcement Branch chief Shafilliza Samsuri said various medicines without Health Ministry approval were seized from the premises.
"These clinics targeted foreign customers.
"The modus operandi detected was that the premises were suspected of being operated by foreign doctors. However, no one was inside the premises during the raid.
"Initial investigations found that patients would be brought to rooms at the back of the premises to undergo blood pressure and blood sugar tests before being given medication," she told reporters.
Shafilliza said the medicines seized included antibiotics and drugs used to treat high blood pressure and fungal infections.
Authorities also discovered injectable local anaesthetics and sets of needles at the premises.
She said most of the medicines were believed to have been brought into Malaysia from Bangladesh.
"We will investigate who rented the premises and identify the individual who acted as the doctor," she said.
The operation was conducted by the Immigration Department together with the Health Ministry, Companies Commission of Malaysia (SSM), Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, Kuala Lumpur City Hall and National Registration Department.
Meanwhile, SSM issued 25 compounds totalling RM66,500 following inspections at 125 premises during the operation.
Among the offences detected were failures to display business names and registration numbers on signboards, official receipts, bills and invoices, as well as failures to display business registration certificates at the premises.
Other offences included failing to submit particulars of changes to businesses as required under the Registration of Businesses Act 1956 and Companies Act 2016.
SSM will also take action under Section 5C of the Registration of Businesses Act 1956 and Section 549 of the Companies Act 2016 over the alleged misuse of business registrations by allowing foreigners to operate businesses.
The Kuala Lumpur Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry also issued 10 compounds totalling RM8,500 for offences involving pricing and weighing instruments.
Enforcement officers also seized 119kg of subsidised packet cooking oil for further investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid has 3 options to challenge unity government
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Abdul Karim said Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has three options if he wishes to challenge the unity government without waiting for the prime minister to take action to remove the party from the coalition.
He said the three options were for Umno and Barisan Nasional (BN) MPs to withdraw their support for the government, for Umno ministers to resign from Cabinet, or to table a motion of no confidence against the prime minister when Parliament sits on Oct 5.
He said all three options had parliamentary channels available and did not require Zahid to wait for Anwar to dismiss Umno ministers or remove the party from the government.
"The unity government is not a formal coalition — it is a loose arrangement and any party can withdraw at any time. At the same time, Anwar is someone who is indebted to Umno and would not have the heart to dismiss Umno ministers or remove the party from the government.
"It is unbecoming to be making threats and issuing challenges at the 2026 Umno General Assembly because the people are watching. It would be better to follow the example of Pandan MP Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli, who resigned on his own accord.
"Zahid may crow in front of three million Umno members, but do not forget the country has 33 million citizens," he said when contacted today.
Yesterday, media reports said Umno had issued an ultimatum to the unity government: either call the 16th general election to seek a fresh mandate, or formally remove Umno from the coalition.
Zahid said the call was made after taking into account demands that Umno should no longer remain part of the unity government.
Meanwhile, Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) Faculty of Administrative Science and Policy Studies senior political science lecturer Mujibu Abd Muis said if the relationship ended and a majority could no longer be maintained, the dissolution of Parliament could become an option to seek a new mandate.
"However, government support is still estimated at around 120 seats if BN withdraws its support. That figure still exceeds the 112 seats needed for a simple majority, but the margin of only around eight seats cannot be considered comfortable.
"From a purely numerical standpoint, Anwar can still survive without BN, provided PH, GPS and GRS and other government supporters remain committed. The question is not just whether BN leaves, but whether Anwar can consistently maintain at least 112 votes through to GE16, particularly when passing the budget and other important government business," he said.
He added that the roles of GPS and GRS would become significantly more important as both held around 30 seats each, comparable in size to BN based on the current composition.
"But if GPS and GRS also withdraw their support, the government would lose another 30 seats and the number could fall to around 90 seats. At that point, the government would no longer have a simple majority. GPS and GRS would therefore no longer be mere coalition partners but would become among the key kingmakers in determining the survival of the government.
"The decisions of both parties are not necessarily determined by the national ideology of Umno, Pas or PH alone. The main factors are the implementation of MA63, state powers and autonomy, development allocations, infrastructure projects, state revenues, the position of Sabah and Sarawak in the federal government and the stability of the relationship between Putrajaya and the state governments.
"Sabah and Sarawak are no longer merely appendages of the federal government but have growing bargaining power as Peninsular Malaysia faces intense political competition," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PKNPk sharpens pupils' digital skills
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Perak State Development Corp (PKNPk) continues to strengthen digital literacy and modern media skills among primary school students through its StratCom Jr. Programme.
The programme, conducted in collaboration with Sekolah Kebangsaan St. Michael (SKSMI), Ipoh, aims to equip students and teachers with digital communication, critical thinking and media production skills.
PKNPk chief executive Datuk Redza Rafiq Abdul Razak said early exposure to media and communication skills was important in building a strong foundation in media literacy and critical thinking.
"We want the new generation to see technology as more than just a medium for accessing information or entertainment. They also need to know how to use it wisely, think critically and communicate responsibly.
"That is what we are seeking to develop through the StratCom Jr. programme. It starts with simple skills, but the foundations being built are important in preparing them for future demands," he said in a statement.
PKNPk said the collaboration, which began in 2024, is being implemented in phases through professional guidance and advisory support to help students develop capabilities in managing digital communications and producing structured, creative and effective content.
To ensure that the skills gained can be put into practice, PKNPk also contributed an iPhone 15 together with a set of media accessories to SKSMI.
The contribution will support the school's media team in producing higher-quality digital content and documenting various school activities.
For PKNPk, state development is not solely about building industries, attracting investments or creating economic opportunities, but extends to supporting talent development and people-centric initiatives.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mujahid ready to assist MACC probe into Tabung Haji RCI findings
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Former minister Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa said he was ready to assist investigations into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
He said, however, that he had yet to receive any official notice from the
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
Mujahid, who was the minister overseeing religious affairs in 2018, said he had no problem providing investigators with whatever information he knew about the issues raised in the RCI report.
"I have been ready for a long time. There is no problem. If they want to ask me what I know, I am open to it," he told reporters after speaking at the RCI TH #Stand4RCITH information programme here today.
He said assisting an investigation could take different forms, including being called to provide information or attend an inquiry at a particular location, but he had so far received no official notice for either.
Mujahid, who is also Amanah deputy president, said nearly half of the 14 cases referred for action in the RCI report had already been known when he headed the ministry in 2018, during efforts to rehabilitate TH.
"Almost half of the 14 cases were already known when I was leading the ministry in 2018, and police reports had been lodged then," he said.
He said cases that had reached the courts should be allowed to take their legal course without political interference.
"We do not interfere in court cases. That is the legal process which we leave to the courts and prosecutors, and we respect it," he said.
Mujahid said the nationwide #Stand4RCITH programme was aimed at helping the public understand the lessons from the RCI findings and addressing confusion surrounding the report, rather than interfering in ongoing legal proceedings.
"What is important is that we learn from this so that similar things do not happen again.
"We also need to explain the confusion that has been raised. That is our responsibility through this nationwide tour, while defending the credibility of the RCI report," he said.
The disclosure of the
RCI findings
on TH's management and operations in July triggered a series of investigations and legal action against individuals identified in connection with the findings.
As of today, four people have been charged in court, while several others, including former senior TH executives and a former minister, have been detained and remanded to assist investigations.
Also present at today's programme were Johor Amanah chairman Aminolhuda Hassan, Johor Amanah deputy chairman Suhaizan Kayat and former Johor Legislative Assembly Speaker Datuk Dr Mohd Puad Zarkashi.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Study hard, become a doctor': Daughter remembers late mother's advice
Article:
KUCHING: Fifteen-year-old Euodia Then Suling is drawing strength from her late mother's advice to study hard and pursue her dream of becoming a doctor following Tuesday's fatal helicopter crash in Long Lellang.
Her mother, Flying Doctor Service (FDS) nurse Debra Moset, was among five people killed.
The Form Three student of Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Penrissen No. 1 said she last saw her mother on Sept 3 at Kampung Semadang, several days before the crash.
"I once told my mother that I really wanted to become a doctor, and she told me that I had to study hard and achieve that dream," she said when met while receiving her mother's remains at the family home in Kampung Semadang, Padawan.
Also present were Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Dr Sim Kui Hian and Sarawak Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Dr Jerip Susil.
Euodia said she had sent her mother a WhatsApp message at 2.30pm on the day of the incident, but it had not been read.
She said she sent another message at 3.40pm, but it showed only one tick.
"In the message, I asked my mother whether she would be coming home for my birthday next month. But she did not reply. It turned out that they had already crashed," she said.
Euodia said she cried when she first learned about the disaster and could not believe her mother was gone, as she continued to hope that she might have survived.
"I hoped my mother was still alive because some people claimed on social media that she had managed to jump out," she said.
The tragedy on Sept 8 involved a BO-105 helicopter operating the FDS while carrying out a healthcare mission.
Five people
aboard the helicopter were killed — pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and nurses Debra, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44.
Meanwhile, Euodia's 12-year-old brother, Eugene Then Kuling, said he had accompanied his mother to the airport on Sept 3.
He said his mother did not give him any specific message, but he vividly remembered her waving goodbye.
"She only waved at me before entering the departure area at Kuching International Airport," he said.
Debra will be buried at St Patrick's Cemetery in Kampung Semadang, Padawan, tomorrow.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Timber exports reach RM9.4 bln for January-June 2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's timber industry continues to contribute significantly to exports, reaching RM9.4 billion between January and June 2026, while its average annual export value exceeds RM20 billion.
Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad said the industry is no longer focused only on timber production and processing.
It has expanded into the production of furniture, doors, flooring, building components, interior finishes and various lifestyle products.
Agarwood, produced from the karas tree, is another high-value commodity in the sector, she said.
"Its unique aroma makes agarwood an important ingredient in the production of essential oils, fragrances and premium products.
"Today, more than two million karas trees have been planted nationwide," she said in her closing speech at the Road to the Oud and Wood Artisan Expo (OWA) with Commodities Programme and the pre-launch of OWA 2027 today.
Noraini said a more organised agarwood industry, starting with cultivation, resin production, processing, product development and marketing, should be developed leveraging this foundation.
She said agarwood has an established market with considerable room for growth.
"But we do not want to remain as a raw material exporter only.
"We want to move from wood to essential oils, from essential oils to fragrances, and subsequently to premium brands that carry Malaysia's name," she said.
The production of agarwood oil, perfumes, personal care products, handicrafts, souvenirs and various lifestyle products offers opportunities for local entrepreneurs to enter higher-value segments of the value chain.
"Agarwood is more than just wood or a traditional fragrance ingredient. It embodies heritage, craftsmanship, innovation and immense commercial value," she said.
Noraini said the development of the industry must benefit the entire value chain, from karas tree growers and distillers to artisans, product manufacturers, brand owners and exporters.
Combining natural resources with artisanal skills, innovation, design, and branding could establish Malaysian agarwood as one of the nation's key identities, she said, adding that broader market access underpins this potential.
"Malaysian agarwood oil has been used as a key ingredient in the production of luxury fragrances by international brands. This proves that our products can go much further," she said.
Noraini said the Road to OWA initiative brings the local agarwood, timber and handicraft industries closer to the public. It also showcases other agricultural commodities such as palm oil, rubber, cocoa, pepper and kenaf.
The programme is not only a platform for exhibitions and sales, but also brings producers, artisans and entrepreneurs together with industry partners and markets, she said.
"This is the first step towards elevating local heritage and skills through the production of high-value products that have the potential to reach wider markets," she said.

Title: Governance,  monitoring still key issues seven years after Sungai Kim Kim
Article:
LETTERS:
Seven years after the Sungai Kim Kim chemical pollution disaster, the latest High Court ruling brings some measure of accountability to those affected.
Four defendants have been found liable in the civil claims brought by 171 plaintiffs, while the question of damages will be dealt with separately.
It is an important development. But as we look at what happened in 2019, perhaps we should ask a bigger question: what have we actually learned?
The New Straits Times reported that residents had raised concerns about suspicious discharges as far back as 2012, while monitoring later showed how badly the river had deteriorated.
A good safety system should not wait until people are falling ill before it starts asking what went wrong.
The Academy of Sciences Malaysia identified weaknesses in chemical governance and uncontrolled industrial growth, and recommended measures such as real-time gas detection, revised safety buffer zones and stronger local environmental monitoring.
Malaysia has also strengthened environmental penalties. These are important steps, and they should not be dismissed.
But rules and penalties alone do not make a system safe. What matters is whether we can spot a hazardous situation early, whether the information reaches the people who can act on it, and whether someone actually does.
A parliamentary discussion earlier this year again raised concerns about post-approval monitoring, coordination between agencies and the combined impact of industrial activities in the same area. Seven years after Sungai Kim Kim, these are not old questions.
We should also remember that the people affected by Sungai Kim Kim did not get to move on simply because the emergency ended. For some, health and economic consequences have continued for years.
The latest court proceedings themselves remind us that compensation and recovery can take much longer than the news cycle.
That is why I believe we need to know whether the changes made after 2019 are actually making our communities safer. Are we detecting problems earlier?
Are agencies sharing information quickly enough? Are we looking at the combined risks around heavily industrialised areas, rather than treating each facility as though it exists on its own?
These are not unreasonable questions. They are the questions we should be asking if we genuinely want to learn from what happened and most importantly, avoid a recurrence.
DR MARZIAH ZAHAR
Senior academic
Safety, Health and Environmental
Universiti Utara Malaysia

Title: Illegal immigrants scramble, struggle with authorities as 472 detained in crackdown [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Foreigners scrambled to escape, locked themselves inside premises and even struggled with enforcement officers as authorities descended on Lebuh Pudu in a massive crackdown today.
By the time the operation ended, 472 undocumented foreigners had been detained after some 2,500 people were screened in the multi-agency operation led by the Kuala Lumpur Immigration Department.
The operation also uncovered an upper-floor premises suspected of being used as a prostitution den, as well as a premises where a bogus doctor was treating foreign patients.
Several locked business premises and workers' hostels had to be forced open before enforcement officers could enter and conduct checks.
The operation, dubbed Op Bersepadu Mega, began at 11am and involved the Immigration Department, National Registration Department, Companies Commission of Malaysia, Fire and Rescue Department, Kuala Lumpur City Hall, Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry and Health Ministry.
The normally busy area descended into chaos when some foreigners attempted to flee in all directions after realising that enforcement teams had moved in.
Some were seen struggling with Immigration officers as they tried to break free.
Kuala Lumpur Immigration director Datuk Hamsha Injau said 2,500 foreigners were screened during the operation.
He said 472 people suspected of being undocumented foreigners were detained, comprising 439 men and 33 women aged between 18 and 62.
"The detainees included nationals from Bangladesh, India, Myanmar, Nepal, China, Pakistan and Zimbabwe.
"Among the main offences detected were failure to possess valid identification documents and overstaying," he told reporters after the operation.
Asked whether Lebuh Pudu was considered a hotspot for undocumented foreigners, Hamsha did not deny this.
He said checks showed that the area attracted large numbers of foreigners during weekends.
"Kuala Lumpur is a focal point for foreigners from various states. Many possess valid travel documents and are working here.
"Since today is a weekend, the area became a gathering point and we screened quite a large number of people.
"From those checks, we found 472 people who did not possess valid documents," he said.
Among those detained was an Indonesian woman in her 20s who claimed she had been working at an online gambling outlet in the area.
"I was detained together with my friend. I have been working here for eight months. My boss pays me RM1,800 a month.
"Most of the customers here are foreigners. The shop opens every day from 9am until 9pm," she said.
Following the large-scale arrests, many premises in the area were left deserted.
Some foreigners were also seen attempting to evade enforcement officers by pretending to be customers at money-changing outlets.
Hamsha said all those detained were taken to the Bukit Jalil Immigration Depot.

Title: Piranha in Klau Dam? Pahang Fisheries investigates
Article:
KUANTAN: The Pahang Fisheries Department is investigating reports that an angler had caught an invasive red-bellied piranha in the Klau Dam in Raub.
Its director, Roslan Abu Hasan, said the department's West Pahang office would visit the dam to gather more information and verify the discovery of the fish, which is commonly found in the Amazon River Basin in South America.
"We will verify the claims about the presence of the species at Klau Dam. Fisheries officers will go there this week," he said in a text message today.
Yesterday, a local freshwater monitoring group raised concerns over the presence of the red-bellied piranha (Pygocentrus nattereri) after red-bellied pacus (Piaractus brachypomus) was previously caught at the dam.
The red-bellied piranha is believed to have been released into the dam.
The presence of the species has raised concerns that more could have been released into the dam or that it could potentially breed there.
Piranhas and pacus, including the red-bellied piranha and red-bellied pacu, are controlled or prohibited species in Malaysia due to concerns over their potential impact as invasive species.
The possession, import or sale of such species is subject to Fisheries Department regulations and approval.
Described as an omnivorous scavenger, the red-bellied piranha is far less aggressive than its reputation suggests and feeds on smaller fish, insects and plant matter.

Title: Make workplace safety and mental health a Budget 2027 priority
Article:
LETTERS:
As Malaysia prepares for Budget 2027, it is imperative that we prioritise the well-being of our workforce by empowering the private sector to embrace occupational safety, health, and mental wellness as core pillars of productivity and sustainability.
The post-pandemic landscape has underscored the urgent need for resilient workplaces that safeguard both physical and psychological health. Budget 2027 presents a timely opportunity to catalyze this transformation through targeted fiscal measures and policy support.
Proposed Tax Incentives
To encourage proactive investment in workplace safety and mental health, the following tax incentives should be considered:
Accelerated Capital Allowance (ACA):
For companies investing in ergonomic equipment, safety systems, and mental health infrastructure such as quiet rooms, wellness pods, or digital therapy platforms.
Double Tax Deduction:
For expenses related to Certified occupational safety and health (OSH) training programs
•  Mental health awareness campaigns
•  Employee assistance programs (EAPs)
•  Hiring of certified OSH officers or workplace counsellors
Tax Relief for SMEs:
Special relief for small and medium enterprises that implement basic OSH standards or mental health support mechanisms, recognizing their limited resources.
Incentives for Preventive Health Screenings:
Tax deductions for companies that offer annual health screenings, stress assessments, or burnout prevention programs.
Other Strategic Measures
Beyond tax incentives, Budget 2027 could introduce complementary initiatives to embed a culture of safety and wellness:
Matching Grants:
For companies adopting internationally recognized OSH certifications (e.g., ISO 45001) or mental health frameworks.
National OSH Innovation Fund:
To support R&D in safety technologies, wearable health monitors, and AI-driven risk assessments.
Public-Private Partnerships:
To co-develop training modules, toolkits, and digital platforms for mental health literacy and hazard prevention.
Mandatory Reporting & Benchmarking:
Encourage voluntary disclosure of OSH and mental health metrics, with incentives for top-performing companies.
Recognition Programs:
Establish national awards for exemplary employers in OSH and mental wellness, fostering healthy competition and visibility.
Budget 2027 must reflect our collective commitment to building humane, safe, and future-ready workplaces. By incentivizing the private sector to lead in this space, we not only protect lives—we unlock higher engagement, lower absenteeism, and stronger economic resilience.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
CHAIRMAN
ALLIANCE FOR A SAFE COMMUNITY

Title: Malaysians lose RM2.97bil to online scams
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians lost RM2.97 billion to online scams last year, Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said.
Rusdi said the trend was global and constantly evolving with technology, with syndicates increasingly using artificial intelligence (AI) to deceive victims.
"The war against scams cannot be won by the police alone.
"It will be won when law enforcement agencies, banks, digital platforms, telecommunications companies and every citizen act as a team," he said when contacted today.
Rusdi said online crime was no longer limited to conventional methods but had evolved into highly organised operations with specialised roles, from preparing scripts and gathering victims' data to laundering money through mule accounts and cryptocurrencies.
"These syndicates exploit human psychology, particularly through fear and greed, to manipulate victims into transferring funds hastily without verifying the request.
"The perception that highly educated people are not vulnerable to such risks is misplaced, as syndicates are now using highly convincing AI technology to target people from all walks of life," he said.
To tackle this cross-border threat, Rusdi said an integrated approach involving four key pillars was important: enforcement agencies, the banking system, digital platforms and public awareness.
"People are urged to remain sceptical at all times and not disclose banking information to unknown parties.
"If they fall victim, the public are advised to immediately contact the National Scam Response Centre at 997 so that swift action can be taken to freeze the account before the funds are transferred overseas," he said.

Title: Nepal floods: After 19 days, families of missing Malaysians hope for a miracle
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The families of 55 Malaysians still unaccounted for after the Nepal flood disaster are clinging to hope of a miracle, even as 19 days have passed since the tragedy struck.
Hani Othman, wife of Port Klang Fire and Rescue Station operations officer Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, known affectionately as Loe, said authorities had yet to provide any update on the DNA matching process involving family members in Malaysia and victim samples in Nepal.
She said the family understood that the process was still ongoing and hoped those yet to be located would be found safe.
"There's no update (on the DNA matching). But we were told it is still in progress.
"I am still hoping for a miracle, but I have made peace with whatever is decided," she said when contacted today.
Hani reportedly flew to Kathmandu on Aug 28 on her own initiative to get first-hand updates on the search operation for her husband and other victims who remained uncontactable following the disaster in Nepal.
She said the decision was made because she wanted to be closer to the search operation rather than wait for updates from Malaysia.
Asked about Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan's statement that the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (MAS-01) was expected to return home yesterday or today after concluding its search and rescue mission in Nepal, Hani said she was not prepared to comment on the matter for now.
"I don't know how to comment on that. I have to be mindful of many parties, this is a very sensitive issue," she said.
Meanwhile, P Sivan, 72, father of Rajita Sivan, said the family's DNA samples had been taken and they were now awaiting further developments from the Foreign Ministry.
He said the family hoped the victims' bodies could be found so that DNA matching could be carried out and their identities confirmed.
"DNA has been taken. Waiting for news from the Foreign Ministry. I hope she can be found so DNA (matching) can be done. If she is found (alive), it will be a miracle," he said.
Fifty-five Malaysians remain unaccounted for following the disaster, while 77 others who were found safe in Tibet and Nepal have been brought to Kathmandu to complete the necessary procedures before returning to Malaysia.

Title: Four agencies to support medical flights in remote Sarawak - Dzulkefly

Title: China, Russia, India seek economic cooperation at BRICS
Article:
New Delhi: BRICS leaders including China, Russia and India entered a second day of talks in New Delhi on Sunday, discussing "inclusive global growth", after reaching rare agreement calling for calm in the Middle East.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for "cooperation" within the bloc, which he has said represents "50 percent of the world's population, 40 percent of global GDP and more than 25 percent of global trade."
"The power of BRICS lies in our diversity and cooperation," Modi told leaders, including Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, on the final day of talks.
BRICS was created in 2009 as a forum for major emerging economies seeking greater influence in institutions dominated by Western powers. The group is seeking to bolster its global influence and address conflict, trade turbulence and energy security.
"We have tried to push inclusive global growth," Modi said.
"We may be rooted in different realities, but together we rise through cooperation and blossom for humanity," he said.
- 'Maximum restraint' -
The first day of the summit on Saturday was dominated by the conflict in the Middle East.
BRICS foreign ministers had failed to agree on a joint statement in New Delhi in May, with Iran, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates divided over the war that began with US-Israeli strikes on February 28.
However, leaders – who also included Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian – issued a statement after intense diplomatic efforts by host India.
"We express deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in Middle East/West Asia," the joint statement said, adding that the BRICS countries "call for exercising maximum restraint."
Modi maintains cordial relations with both Iran and US ally Israel, but is also careful to strike a delicate balance in India's ties with Washington.
India has navigated the energy crisis caused by the US-Iran war in part by turning to Russia, despite Moscow's war in Ukraine and pressure from Washington and other Western capitals.
- 'Advancing together' -
Xi's participation in BRICS is also important because it is his first visit to neighbouring India since 2019, and the biggest step yet in a cautious thaw between the nuclear-armed rivals.
His visit comes six years after a deadly military clash along the disputed Tibetan border between China and India, with ties gradually improving through restored flights, visas and high-level contacts.
"Although our two countries are different in many respects, they are fully capable of complementing each other's strengths, supporting one another, achieving mutual success and advancing together," Xi said as he met Modi, according to a video released by New Delhi.
The underlying territorial dispute remains unresolved, and both sides retain heavy military deployments along their roughly 3,500-kilometre (2,175-mile) high-altitude border.
India's foreign ministry said in a statement after the meeting that "the two leaders expressed commitment to a fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question."
Deep mistrust remains, with a widening trade deficit and strategic rivalry complicating ties.
"Both sides should... work hand-in-hand to promote high-quality major financial cooperation, advocate an equal and sustainable global order, and foster an economic globalisation that is open and inclusive," Xi said.
Xi's visit was the target of protests by dozens of Tibetans in New Delhi, exiles like their Buddhist leader, the Dalai Lama, who has lived in India since fleeing a Chinese crackdown in 1959.

Title: 3 Penang policemen remanded over alleged extortion
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Three policemen have been remanded for four days to assist investigations into an alleged extortion incident in Pulau Tikus on Aug 6.
The remand order, which runs until Wednesday (Sept 16), was issued by magistrate Siti Nurul Suhaila Baharin for the suspects, aged between 30 and 48, who hold the ranks of sergeant, lance corporal and constable.
The remand was sought to facilitate investigations under Section 384 of the Penal Code.
The trio were arrested in separate raids carried out from yesterday until early this morning at several locations in the state.
Their arrests followed a police report lodged by a man who claimed that he and three cousins had gone to Jalan Ladang Hong Seng, Pulau Tikus, to look for a friend's relative who was allegedly detained by police.

The man claimed that they were handcuffed and threatened with being implicated in a Telekom Malaysia cable theft case unless they handed over RM20,000.

Title: [UPDATED] Fertiliser company managing director arrested over Baja 3 distribution delays
Article:
ALOR STAR: The managing director of a fertiliser supply company has been arrested over delays in the distribution of supplementary compound fertiliser, known as Baja 3, to padi farmers in Kedah.
He was arrested after turning up at the Kedah Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) office to have his statement recorded at about 2.30pm yesterday.
The man, who is in his 30s, was remanded until Sept 16 after Magistrate Eliana Ismail allowed the MACC's application at the magistrate's court here this morning.
Kedah MACC director Datuk Nazli Rasyid Sulong, when contacted, confirmed the arrest and said the case was being investigated under Section 18 of the MACC Act 2009.
The provision covers offences involving the submission of documents containing false particulars with the intention of deceiving a principal.
It was reported that the failure to deliver 282,360 bags of fertiliser to about 60,000 padi farmers forms
part of the MACC's probe
into supply delays in Kedah.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman had said that initial investigations revealed that Taaveekun Manufacturing Sdn Bhd was required to supply 616,015 bags of additional compound fertiliser, known as Baja 3, during the first planting season.
However, only 333,655 bags had been delivered as of September, leaving a shortfall of 282,360 bags.
The company was appointed by the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry to supply, deliver and distribute additional compound fertiliser, known as Baja Padi 3, under the Padi Production Incentive Scheme (SIPP).
The contract covers the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada) area,
spanning 100,000ha
and involving about 60,000 padi farmers.
It was also reported that the Agriculture and Food Security Minister and senior ministry officials could be called up by MACC as it widens its probe into the delays.
Investigators had been instructed to conduct a
comprehensive probe
covering everyone involved in the policy, tender and implementation of the supply process.
Earlier this week, MACC opened an investigation paper into delays in the distribution of supplementary compound fertiliser, known as Baja 3, to padi farmers in Kedah.
The commission said its Kedah office received a complaint from Pertubuhan Persaudaraan Pesawah Malaysia (Pesawah) on Aug 26 and opened an investigation into the matter.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had previously expressed his dissatisfaction over the delays, which he said had affected farmers who had raised their concerns and submitted memoranda to him.
He had said that the government needed to determine the cause, including identifying the company entrusted with the distribution and whether it had fulfilled its obligations.
